$comment: Mirror of manifest/litertlm_manifest.schema.json in the hf-to-litertlm repository, for the manifest_schema 0.1 line. Keep the two in sync.
title: litertlm deployment manifest
description:
litertlm_manifest.json sits at the root of a Hugging Face model repo that ships .litertlm bundles for the LiteRT-LM runtime. It describes every bundle in the repo: the backends each file is verified on, which file a device should pick, what it requires, and how fast it measured.
https://github.com/john-rocky/hf-to-litertlm/blob/main/manifest/SCHEMA.md

manifest_schema.description: Version of the manifest format. The 0.1 line is the compatibility line: a 0.1.x release only adds optional fields, so a 0.2 manifest is rejected rather than half-parsed.

repo.description: Hugging Face repo id (owner/name) the manifest lives in. Together with a variant's file name this is the download address.

variants.description: One entry per .litertlm file in the repo.

speed.description: A measured value: a number, or a "lo-hi" range string when the runs spread (CPU rows on phones spread with thermal throttling).

channelMarkers.description: Exact marker strings of a channel, whitespace included.

declaredChannel.description: One entry of the bundle's declared channel set (manifest 0.1.1 and later).

name.description: Channel name as declared in the bundle header.

is_reasoning.description: True when the bundle marks this channel as its reasoning channel.

capabilities.description: Capability flags derived from the bundle header, so they are readable before download.

vision.description: Derived: the bundle declares image input.

audio.description: Derived: the bundle declares audio input.

thinking.description: Derived: whether the bundle declares a thinking channel, and its markers. Mirrors the first declared channel.

declared.description: True when the bundle declares a channel.

channels.description: Derived (manifest 0.1.1 and later): the bundle's full declared channel set, whether thinking, tool-call, or anything else the model declares.

sessionDefaults.description: Curated session knobs a wrapper should set that the engine cannot infer. An open object: readers take keys by name and ignore what they do not consume.

max_output_tokens_min.description: A floor on the output-token budget (e.g. 2048 for reasoning models), never a cap.

notes.description: Curated guidance worth surfacing to the app developer.

model.description: Model-level facts. Fields marked Derived are read out of the bundle header by the generator; the rest are curated.

base_model.description: Hugging Face id of the source model.

license.description: SPDX identifier, or a pointer to the license file.

recommendation.description: The fastest verified backend for a platform, optionally narrowed to a device class.

device_class.description: Free-text device class the recommendation applies to, e.g. "midrange" or "flagship".

backend.description: Backend to use on this platform. Must be one of the variant's verified backends; resolvers ignore a recommendation naming an unlisted backend.

reason.description: Why this backend wins on this platform, in words that carry the evidence.

requirements.description: What the variant needs beyond the runtime version.

peak_ram_mb.description: Peak resident memory observed while generating, in megabytes.

platform_notes.description: Platform caveats to surface to the app developer.

measuredRow.description: One measured performance row. Every row states its conditions and its provenance; rows come from generation-verified backends only.

device.description: Device the row was measured on, e.g. "Pixel 8a (Tensor G3)".

backend.description: Backend the row was measured on.

runtime.description: LiteRT-LM release and build the row was measured with.

prefill_tps.description: Prefill throughput in tokens per second.

decode_tps.description: Decode throughput in tokens per second.

ttft_s.description: Time to first token in seconds.

cache.description: Whether a compiled-model cache was in use. "no" means a cold compile; caches mask load regressions and inflate disk cost.

runs.description: Number of runs the row summarizes.

source.description: Provenance of the numbers: which log or model-card table they come from.

evidence.description: Pointer to the primary log. Stripped from published manifests and kept in the converter's own records.

section.description: Derived: one row of the bundle's section table.

type.description: Section data type as named in the bundle header, e.g. "LlmMetadataProto", "HF_Tokenizer_Zlib" or "TFLiteModel".

model_type.description: The section's model_type item when present, e.g. "tf_lite_prefill_decode" or "tf_lite_embedder".

backend_constraint.description: The section's backend_constraint item when present: a comma-separated list of backends the engine will load it on.

variant.description: One .litertlm file. Fields marked Derived are read from Hub metadata or the bundle header; the rest are curated and carry evidence.

sha256.description: Derived: SHA-256 of the file from Hub LFS metadata. Verify after download.

quantization.description: Quantization recipe, stated honestly, e.g. "int4 block-32 linears, fp32 activations".

backends.description: Backends this file is verified to generate on, not merely load. A resolver never returns a backend absent from this list.

default_backend.description: Backend to pick with no device knowledge.

min_runtime_version.description: Earliest LiteRT-LM release the file is verified on, e.g. "0.15.0".

recommended.description: The fastest verified choice per platform and device class.

measured.description: Measured performance rows with conditions and provenance.

known_issues.description: Short, factual known issues, with upstream links where they exist.
